site.title: THE WALL THAT SAID HELP
site.subtitle: A Free Investigation Into the Wooden Horse Nobody Checked

site.heroCaption: EXHIBIT 0: The city of the siege. Every red pin is a proof. Every ringed shield is a clue. Click a pin. Click a shield. LOOK.
intro: The teacher said, 'Find Waldo.' The book said, 'Find Waldo.' So I found the big picture with the wooden horse, and I looked.

Night 36. Thirty-one nights on the beach, one each for the rest of the folder, and now this ONE city. Somewhere around 2 AM I stopped asking WHERE he is and started asking the question nobody wants you to ask: ==why does the wall say HELP and then laugh at itself?==

Every proof below has a SEE FOR YOURSELF button. I am not asking you to trust me. I am asking you to LOOK. ~~I'm not crazy.~~ The beach had a postcard. This city has a horse, and nobody in the crowd is checking what's inside it.
Start with the wall. It always starts with the wall.
site.censusInstructions: Click every ringed, banded, or numbered shield in the city above, and the one striped tunic.

claims.title: THE WALL ASKS FOR HELP

facts.text: Outlined white letters spelling HELP sit just above a row of teal wall stones, under the wooden horse.
Three HA groups are printed across the crowd further down, in a row.

claims.leap: A cry for help that laughs three times is not a cry. It is a ==password==. Nobody on that wall needs rescuing. He is the rescue party, handed out at the gate one HA at a time.

update.text: I read the wall eleven times. It still says HELP. It still laughs. CONVENIENT.

claims.alt: The word HELP in outlined white letters, just above the teal wall stones, under the wooden horse.
claims.caption: the wall. it asked first.

claims.title: THE PRICE OF A SHIELD

facts.text: Three round shields in the crowd are printed 76%, 101%, and 41%.
Three round shields a little higher up in the same crowd carry dollar signs.

claims.leap: Nobody prices a shield unless somebody is buying shields. A shield cannot be ==101%== of itself. That is an overage, and overages happen when the same uniform is handed out twice and nobody can say which one is the original.

update.text: UPDATE: I counted the percent signs twice. 101 is over 100. You cannot be over 100 of yourself. Same wall, different currency. See Proof #1.

claims.alt: Round crowd shields printed with 76%, 101%, and 41%, and three shields with dollar signs above them.
claims.caption: they are not discounts.

links.label: THE WALL WANTED HELP. IT ALSO GOT INVOICED.

claims.title: A GIFT NOBODY CHECKED

facts.text: The wooden horse is built from slatted planks and stands above the rooftops.
A helmeted man is climbing up its side.

claims.leap: A gift at the gate that nobody checked. Nobody asked what it was carrying. This is how Waldo gets in: wrapped, unchecked, and in pieces, one plank at a time. Look at the wall, then look at the horse. ==Same instructions.==

update.text: The horse is hollow. I can't prove it. That's the point. Nobody can prove what's inside a gift, and that is exactly what a gift is for.

claims.alt: A large wooden horse of slatted planks rising above the rooftops, with a helmeted man climbing its side.
claims.caption: the gift. the gate. the box.

claims.title: THE SAME SHIELD IN TWO COLOURS

facts.text: A round shield with a black field and concentric white rings.
A round shield with a red field and concentric rings, the same design.

claims.leap: Same shield, two colourways. He is not one man in one shield. The shield is the uniform, and the uniform comes in every colour they have in stock. Proof #3 showed you the gift nobody checked. Here is what came with it.

update.text: I checked the rings with a ruler. The red one is not a different shield. It's the same one, in a different mood.

claims.alt: Two round shields side by side: one with a black field and white rings, one with a red field and rings in the same design.
claims.caption: left: black. right: red. same mould.

claims.title: THE BANDS AND THE TRIM

facts.text: A figure stands in a black-and-white banded tunic, with no hat on.
A white tunic with red trim stands in the crowd.

claims.leap: Bands on one man, red trim on another. Two halves of one outfit. Somebody cut the uniform up and handed the stripes to one person and the trim to someone across the crowd, and neither of them was told the other exists.

update.text: The bands are black and white. The trim is red. I keep checking whether that's a coincidence. Every time, the answer gets a little more ==convenient==.

claims.alt: A figure in a black-and-white banded tunic, and a second white tunic trimmed in red.
claims.caption: the bands. the trim. no hat either time.

claims.title: EVERY SUSPECT IS MISSING THE HAT

facts.text: The banded figure's head is bare, with dark hair and no bobble hat.
The diver's head is bare: no hat, no glasses.

claims.leap: The hat is the one piece nobody is wearing. Every suspect is missing it. Hats do not go missing by accident. They go into a box, and the box goes into the horse.

update.text: I compared both heads to the stamp from the beach. Neither has a hat. I'm not saying that means anything. I'm saying it's ==convenient== that neither has a hat.

claims.alt: Two bare heads: one dark-haired figure in a banded tunic, one diver in a red top, neither in a hat.
claims.caption: the missing hat. (the horse has the box.)

claims.title: MATCHING BLUE

facts.text: Several figures stand side by side in matching blue tunics.
Beside them is a black-rimmed oval shield with a white symbol.

claims.leap: Matching tunics, one row. That is what a uniform looks like after it has been cut into pieces and put back together at the gate. Proof #6 says the hat is missing. Proof #7 says where the rest of the set is standing.

update.text: They are standing shoulder to shoulder, like they were issued together. I'm not going to tell you what they're waiting for. I haven't finished my tea.

claims.alt: Several figures in matching blue tunics standing side by side, with a black-rimmed oval shield beside them.
claims.caption: one row. one colour. no hats.

claims.title: THE DIVE NOBODY WATCHES

facts.text: A red-clad figure dives from the rocks into the sea, arms out.
Other figures stand on the rock ledge above the water and do not dive.

claims.leap: Everybody on the rocks is watching the dive. Nobody is watching the horse. The sea has no gate and no guard, and the diver is the only one who leaves without being counted. Look at the bare head in Proof #6.

update.text: Everyone on that ledge is standing. Only one person is in the water, and it's the one in red. I've counted it four times and I still get the same answer.

claims.alt: A red-clad diver leaping from the rocks into the sea, with figures standing on the ledge above.
claims.caption: the dive. the ledge. the audience.

claims.title: SOMEONE IS SENT UP

facts.text: A helmeted man climbs the side of the wooden horse.
A helmeted figure stands on the roof beside a tall spear.

claims.leap: One climbs and one stands beside a spear. That is a shift schedule. Waldo never climbs anything himself. He is sent up, and the one on the roof writes down the time.

update.text: Both of them wear the same helmet. Same helmet, different job. I'm not going to say whose job is worse. I'm just asking the question.

claims.alt: A helmeted man climbing the wooden horse and a helmeted figure on the roof beside a tall spear.
claims.caption: up. and the one with the spear.

claims.title: THE ANSWER WEARS RED

facts.text: A red-clad soldier stands right beside the HELP sign.
The HELP sign sits just above the teal wall stones, directly below the wooden horse.

claims.leap: The cry for help is answered by a man in red, standing right beside it. That is not a rescue. That is the uniform answering its own call. Proof #1 asked for help. Proof #9 says who was sent.

update.text: I don't think he's helping. I think he's the reply. ==I'm not sure what I'm saying.== I am sure about the red.

claims.alt: A red-clad soldier standing right beside the HELP sign, under the wooden horse.
claims.caption: he came when called. in red.

claims.title: THE WARNING AND THE PRICE

facts.text: A round shield on the left side of the city is printed with an exclamation mark.
A shield printed 41% sits in the crowd with the other prices.

claims.leap: There is a warning on the left and a price in the crowd, and they are the same sale. Forty-one percent of him is in stock. The rest is on the horse. Nobody will tell you which piece you bought, because you were never meant to be the buyer.

update.text: Proof #1 says HELP. Proof #2 says 101%. Proof #11 says the exclamation mark is a warning, and I have decided to believe the warning. Going to bed. ~~I am not going to bed.~~

claims.alt: A round shield printed with an exclamation mark and a shield printed 41% in the crowd.
claims.caption: the warning. the price. the same sale.

censusComments: Sixteen. I started with nine. Then I found the rings.
Every shield in the city is a ring if you stare long enough. That's what they're for.
The banded tunic is the only stripe I'd swear to on a person. The shields do the rest.
Why would a shield need a price if it weren't being resold?
Count again. I counted nineteen, then I remembered the wall.

guestbook.name: KaraM_1994
guestbook.text: the horse is a horse. the wall says help because it's a wall painted by a kid. please go to bed
guestbook.reply: Which kid, Kara. WHICH KID. Proof #1 has no kid in it. Look at the letters again. (Proof #1.)

guestbook.name: dorian.k
guestbook.text: the 101% is a sale. 101% just means it's a sale on something that cost more than it did before. thats how i read prices
guestbook.reply: Thank you, Dorian. You are not wrong. You are ==issued==. (See Proof #2.)

guestbook.name: grumpyDad
guestbook.text: i checked. theres no soldier in the horse. theres nothing in the horse. it's wood
guestbook.reply: Of course it's wood. Nobody said it was a soldier. I said it was a gift, and nobody checks a gift. (Proof #3.)

updates.text: Sent the shield prices to a friend in accounting. Their reply: 'nobody prices shields.' I think that is the point.
The bands and the trim are not from the same tailor. I'm sure of it. Same question as the beach postcard: who ordered this?
The horse is still there. The wall still says HELP. I have stopped expecting the picture to change.
Opened the next file in the folder to check something. It is THIS battle. Same horse. Same 76%. Same 101%. They printed the price list twice.

receipts.note: for marking the shields. they don't come marked.
for the wall. I'm not going to say why.
the rings are much smaller than I expected.

lines: Waldo is a horse, a wall, and a row of matching shields.
The wall asks for help. The horse arrives as a gift. The shields come in every colour, and every one of them has a price.
On the wall he is a password. In the crowd he is a row. On the rocks he is a dive nobody watches.
And you have spent your whole life looking for him. Exactly like they wanted.
I'm going to bed. ~~I'm not going to bed.~~
